documents.title: Kennesaw State University Artificial Intelligence Policy
documents.summary: A short institution-wide policy effective May 1, 2026 that sets ethical and security principles for AI-enabled tools, creates an AI Governance Committee to approve tools and maintain a separate Guidance Document, and requires annual AI training. It sets no rules for how students may use AI in coursework.
documents.stance_why: The policy says users 'shall do so ethically, responsibly, and securely' and defers specifics to 'the KSU Institutional Artificial Intelligence Guidance Document'; it states no allow or ban for student coursework, so it delegates.

units.why: The opening sentence sets the university-wide principle that AI-enabled tool users 'shall do so ethically, responsibly, and securely'; it is a framework statement of scope and principle, so P56 (institution-wide framework) fits.

documents.unit: College of Computing and Software Engineering (CCSE), First Year Experience
documents.title: CCSE FYE Policies (Academic Misconduct: AI & Cheating)
documents.summary: The first-year programming page of the computing college says all labs, assignments, quizzes and tests must be written without AI, lists AI use as academic misconduct, and bans AI in exams with penalties up to an F. It applies to the FYE course sequence only.
documents.stance_why: The page requires work 'Written by you, without the use of AI' and states 'Student MAY NOT use AI' on exams, with no exceptions, so it prohibits.
